newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday March 13.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi announced his Forza Italia party will vote against a decree law put forward by Labour Minister Tiziano Treu in order to help ease unemployment. Party had previously said it would simply abstain from voting. Hard-left Communist Refoundation party intends to vote against measures. Prime Minister Romano Prodi says he's amazed at sudden change in Forza Italia stance. (all).

* In an interview, Berlusconi praised Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's recent disapproval of Prodi's overtures to Communist Refoundation, adding that time has come to action. Berlusconi defines Treu's law proposal as "old-fashioned political nonsense", repeating that it is not by legislative means that new jobs can be created (Corriere).

* Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni repeated there was no programme to freeze civil servants' pensions and said Italy's majority coalition will discuss unemployment and not mini-budget today (all).

* Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi confirms board of state-controlled telecoms group Stet to meet on March 14. Ciampi said there will be a "hard core" group of shareholders holding 10 to 15 percent of share capital. Communist Refoundation said it wants to see what "hard core" would be like. (all).

* Italy had a 451 billion lire trade surplus with non-EU countries in January. Italy had a global trade surplus of 4.036 trillion lire in December 1996 against 3.158 trillion lire in December 1995. Augusto Fantozzi, Minister for Foreign Trade, said industry needs backing (all).
* Italian stocks closed lower with losses on other stock markets and weighed by weaker lira and Btp bond futures amid worries over launch of EMU and domestic politics (all).

* Bank of Italy said it has modified capital adequacy requirements for banks and credit institutions, in line with EU directives. Bank of Italy will now take into account consolidated data and not just individual firm's balance sheet (all).
* Ciampi announced Treasury is planning to abolish the mid-month auctions of government bills (Sole 24 Ore).
* Italian commercial vehicle sales fell 5.97 year-on-year in February to 11,774 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
